_about: Language Lab policy every course shares (shown on the LAB folder description and Lab 0). A course can override any of these in its own Course settings. Edited in the website editor › Lab policy. Copied from TeachingOS lab-builder/policy.json on 2026-11-21, with the faculty-approved Excused Absence line.
incomplete_rule: No face or no audio for most of the video: 0 points, and you can't resubmit. Watch your recording before you submit.
responsibility: Making your lab work is your responsibility: your computer, camera, microphone and Bongo, and a video in the required format (face visible, voice clear, and slides shown in slide labs). Complete Lab 0 in the first week, start each lab early, and watch your recording before you submit. A technology problem never extends the deadline, even if you report it before the due time.

lab0.title: Bongo setup check
lab0.summary: A one-minute test recording with your camera and your PowerPoint slides. It unlocks the labs.
lab0.context: Lab 0 checks that your computer can record your camera and your screen at the same time. That is the hardest kind of lab to record, so if Lab 0 works, every lab will. Do it in the first week, so there's time to fix a problem.
slides: Your course and your professor's name
One thing you like (a picture is fine)
lab0.say: Start with *Hola, me llamo…* and your name. The rest can be in English.
checks: Your face is visible the whole time
You shared the window with your slides, not the Bongo tab
lab0.marking: A Lab assistant marks it Complete or Not yet (with a comment) within one business day. Not yet? Fix the problem and submit again. Lab 0 stays open all semester, so you can test a new computer any time.

rubric.name: Speaking rubric

rows.name: Fluency & Discourse
d: Connected sentences joined with linking words; talks to the camera; pauses only to think.
Mostly complete sentences with some linking words; pauses or restarts don't break the message.
A mix of sentences and fragments with long pauses, or flat, list-like delivery with eyes off the camera.
Mostly single words or fragments with long silences, or recited for most of the video.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Comprehensibility & Accuracy
d: Easy to understand throughout; this lab's grammar used correctly.
Understood without effort; this lab's grammar used with a few errors.
Needs a patient listener, or this lab's grammar is missing or often wrong.
Hard to understand even after replaying.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Vocabulary Range
d: Varied: chapter words plus descriptive words and different verbs; rarely repeats; no English.
Chapter vocabulary used correctly, with some variety and description.
A small set of words repeated; little description; some English.
Very few words; frequent English or invented words.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Task Completion
d: Every part answered with specific details; meets the length.
Every part answered; some answers brief; meets the length.
One part missing, or under the length.
Two or more parts missing, or under half the length.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rubric.zero: Nothing to rate (0 in every row): no face or no audio for most of the video, mostly not Spanish, a different lab's task, an edited upload, or a video sent outside Bongo. Bongo needs this column to record a 0.
notes: Notecard: students hold it up to the camera for about 5 seconds at the start. Sentences on the card or the slides: Fluency & Discourse is scored no higher than Does not meet. Rehearsed speech is fine; reading is scored as delivery, not as a separate penalty.
Slides not visible in a slide lab for most of the video (Bongo tab or wrong window shared): Task Completion is scored no higher than Does not meet (2). The speaking rows are scored as usual.
Labs with a video comment: a missing comment counts as one missing part in Task Completion.
Lab 0's Bongo setup check has no rubric: Complete or Not yet, worth 0% of the grade.

system_wide: If the Language Lab or UNG confirms that Bongo or D2L is down for everyone, or a campus closes, the Lab extends the lab for all sections and posts an announcement.
accommodations: Approved accommodations through Student Accessibility Services (SAS)? Contact your professor and your campus Language Lab coordinator at the start of the semester. The coordinator works with SAS directly.
excused: Missed a lab because of an Excused Absence? Contact your professor.
